mustCheck.sign: timing (systolic vs diastolic)
mustCheck.why: First discriminator of the lesion (systolic AS/MR vs diastolic AR/MS).

mustCheck.sign: site of maximal intensity + radiation
mustCheck.why: Localises the valve (AS → carotids; MR → axilla).

mustCheck.sign: character, pitch + intensity (grade)
mustCheck.why: Ejection vs pansystolic vs decrescendo distinguishes lesions; grade aids severity.

mustCheck.sign: dynamic manoeuvres (respiration, hand-grip, squat/stand)
mustCheck.why: Right-sided murmurs ↑ on inspiration; manoeuvres separate AS/HOCM/MR.

mustCheck.sign: peripheral signs of severity (pulse character, pulse pressure, apex, failure signs)
mustCheck.why: Slow-rising/narrow pulse pressure (severe AS), collapsing/wide (severe AR).

ugandaNote: Rheumatic heart disease → mixed/multiple valve lesions are common; characterise EACH murmur; consider infective endocarditis.

mustCheck.sign: apex-radial (pulse) deficit
mustCheck.why: An apical rate exceeding radial confirms AF + ineffective beats.

mustCheck.sign: signs of heart failure (raised JVP, basal crackles, oedema, displaced apex)
mustCheck.why: AF commonly coexists with / precipitates failure.

mustCheck.sign: mitral stenosis signs (loud S1, tapping apex, mid-diastolic murmur)
mustCheck.why: Rheumatic mitral disease is a leading AF cause (high Uganda relevance).

mustCheck.sign: focal neurological deficit (embolic screen)
mustCheck.why: AF is a major cause of cardioembolic stroke.

mustCheck.sign: thyroid status (thyrotoxicosis)
mustCheck.why: A reversible AF driver.

ugandaNote: Rheumatic mitral stenosis + thyrotoxicosis are common, treatable AF causes; anticoagulation monitoring (INR) varies.

mustCheck.sign: JVP waveform + hepatojugular reflux; pulsatile (venous) vs non-pulsatile (SVC obstruction)
mustCheck.why: Waveform (large v waves = TR) + reflux refine the cause.

mustCheck.sign: right/biventricular failure signs (oedema, tender hepatomegaly, basal crackles)
mustCheck.why: Confirms congestion + extent.

mustCheck.sign: pericardial signs (pulsus paradoxus, muffled sounds, rub, Kussmaul's sign)
mustCheck.why: Tamponade / constriction are reversible must-not-miss causes.

ugandaNote: Cor pulmonale (chronic lung disease / TB sequelae) and TB pericarditis are key causes.

mustCheck.sign: apex character (heaving/pressure vs thrusting/volume vs tapping)
mustCheck.why: Pressure overload (AS/HTN) vs volume (AR/MR) vs MS.

mustCheck.sign: heaves + thrills; auscultate for murmurs, S3/S4
mustCheck.why: Identifies the underlying valvular / myocardial lesion.

mustCheck.sign: signs of heart failure
mustCheck.why: Cardiomegaly with a displaced apex often reflects failure.

ugandaNote: Dilated cardiomyopathy (peripartum, HIV-associated) + rheumatic valve disease are common.

when.sign: dullness to percussion at a lung base

mustCheck.sign: breath sounds + vocal resonance over that zone
mustCheck.why: Reduced/absent + reduced VR = effusion; bronchial + increased VR = consolidation.

mustCheck.sign: is it stony dull (effusion) vs dull (consolidation/collapse)?
mustCheck.why: Stony dullness points to pleural fluid.

mustCheck.sign: tracheal position + chest expansion
mustCheck.why: Shift away (large effusion) vs towards (collapse) localises + grades.

mustCheck.sign: added sounds (crackles, pleural rub)
mustCheck.why: Crackles support consolidation; a rub suggests pleural inflammation.

ugandaNote: TB causes both effusion + consolidation; empyema / parapneumonic effusions are common.

mustCheck.sign: vocal resonance / fremitus over the zone
mustCheck.why: Increased VR confirms consolidation (lung conducts sound).

mustCheck.sign: percussion note over the zone
mustCheck.why: Dullness supports consolidation; helps exclude effusion.

mustCheck.sign: crackles + the rest of the respiratory exam
mustCheck.why: Coarse crackles support consolidation; completes the pattern.

ugandaNote: Consolidation is commonly pneumonia or TB (+ PCP in HIV) — correlate with fever, cough, HIV status.

when.sign: reduced chest expansion on one side

mustCheck.sign: tracheal position
mustCheck.why: Shift towards (collapse/fibrosis) vs away (large effusion / tension pneumothorax) localises.

mustCheck.sign: percussion + breath sounds on the affected side
mustCheck.why: Stony-dull+absent (effusion), hyper-resonant+absent (pneumothorax), dull+bronchial (consolidation) define the cause.

mustCheck.sign: full respiratory exam (suppurative / fibrotic / malignant lung disease)
mustCheck.why: Bronchiectasis, abscess/empyema, fibrosis, carcinoma are key thoracic causes.

mustCheck.sign: signs of infective endocarditis / cyanotic heart disease
mustCheck.why: Cardiac causes of clubbing.

mustCheck.sign: signs of chronic liver disease / IBD
mustCheck.why: GI causes.

ugandaNote: Post-TB bronchiectasis + empyema are common Ugandan causes of clubbing.

mustCheck.sign: liver span, edge, surface, consistency, tenderness, pulsatility
mustCheck.why: Span confirms enlargement; craggy/hard = malignancy, tender smooth = congestion/hepatitis, pulsatile = TR.

mustCheck.sign: splenomegaly
mustCheck.why: Hepatosplenomegaly narrows the differential.

mustCheck.sign: ascites (shifting dullness / fluid thrill)
mustCheck.why: Points to portal hypertension / CLD or malignancy.

mustCheck.sign: chronic liver disease signs (jaundice, spider naevi, palmar erythema, caput medusae) + flap
mustCheck.why: Establishes chronicity + decompensation (encephalopathy).

ugandaNote: HCC (hepatitis B, aflatoxin) presents as a hard, tender, rapidly enlarging liver; hepatitis B/C + congestive causes common.

mustCheck.sign: confirm it is spleen (can't get above it, moves with respiration, notch, dull) vs left kidney
mustCheck.why: Distinguishes splenomegaly from a renal mass.

mustCheck.sign: degree of enlargement + hepatomegaly + ascites
mustCheck.why: Massive vs moderate + hepatosplenomegaly narrow the cause.

mustCheck.sign: lymphadenopathy + anaemia/bruising (haematological screen)
mustCheck.why: Lymphoma/leukaemia + haemolysis present with splenomegaly + nodes/anaemia.

ugandaNote: Massive splenomegaly: hyper-reactive malarial splenomegaly, schistosomiasis, CML, lymphoma; early sickle cell.

mustCheck.sign: confirm fluid (fluid thrill / shifting dullness) + exclude the other 'Fs' of distension
mustCheck.why: Confirms fluid vs fat/flatus/faeces/fetus/mass.

mustCheck.sign: chronic liver disease + hepatosplenomegaly + portal hypertension (caput medusae)
mustCheck.why: Differentiates portal-hypertensive ascites.

mustCheck.sign: raised JVP / right heart failure / constrictive pericarditis signs
mustCheck.why: Cardiac ascites is an important reversible cause.

mustCheck.sign: lymphadenopathy / cachexia / fever (malignancy, TB peritonitis)
mustCheck.why: Malignant + tuberculous ascites are common, need specific work-up.

ugandaNote: TB peritonitis + malignancy are common alongside CLD (hepatitis B, schistosomal portal hypertension); diagnostic paracentesis is key.

mustCheck.sign: peritonism (guarding, rebound, percussion tenderness, rigidity)
mustCheck.why: Distinguishes localised tenderness from peritonitis needing urgent surgical review.

mustCheck.sign: bowel sounds + percussion (obstruction / perforation)
mustCheck.why: Absent sounds / board-like rigidity flag perforation; tinkling suggests obstruction.

mustCheck.sign: fever + vitals (sepsis screen) + pregnancy test in reproductive-age women
mustCheck.why: An acute abdomen with sepsis is time-critical; exclude ectopic pregnancy.

ugandaNote: Typhoid ileal perforation + complicated appendicitis are important causes; always consider ectopic pregnancy.
cso_reason: Localised-tenderness follow-ups cross surgical/obstetric pathways; CSO to confirm IM-clerkship scope + the mandatory pregnancy-test prompt.

mustCheck.sign: tone (spastic vs flaccid) in the affected limb(s)
mustCheck.why: ↑ tone = UMN; ↓ tone (+ wasting/fasciculations) = LMN — the localisation step.

mustCheck.sign: deep tendon reflexes + plantar response
mustCheck.why: Brisk + upgoing plantar = UMN; absent = LMN.

mustCheck.sign: power (MRC) + pattern (pyramidal / proximal / distal / single-nerve / hemiparesis)
mustCheck.why: Localises the lesion (cortex/cord/root/plexus/nerve/muscle).

mustCheck.sign: sensory exam incl. a sensory level
mustCheck.why: A sensory level is a red-flag pointer to cord compression (must-not-miss).

mustCheck.sign: coordination + gait (where safe)
mustCheck.why: Adds cerebellar/functional information.

ugandaNote: Stroke, HIV CNS disease, spinal TB (Pott's) + B12 deficiency are key; a sensory level demands urgent cord-compression work-up.

mustCheck.sign: tone + reflexes in the same limb (UMN corroboration)
mustCheck.why: Confirms an UMN lesion (spasticity, hyper-reflexia).

mustCheck.sign: sensory level + spinal exam
mustCheck.why: Localises a cord lesion + screens for compression (must-not-miss).

mustCheck.sign: higher function / cranial nerves (lesion above or below foramen magnum?)
mustCheck.why: Distinguishes a cerebral from a cord cause.

ugandaNote: Pott's disease (spinal TB) + HIV myelopathy are important cord causes — UMN picture + sensory level needs urgent imaging/referral.

mustCheck.sign: plantar response (paradoxically upgoing?)
mustCheck.why: Absent ankle jerks WITH extensor plantars = classic mixed UMN+LMN (B12, MND, dual pathology).

mustCheck.sign: distal sensation (glove-and-stocking) incl. vibration/proprioception
mustCheck.why: Peripheral neuropathy (diabetes, B12, HIV, alcohol) is the common cause.

mustCheck.sign: diabetic-foot / vascular check if neuropathy suspected
mustCheck.why: Links to protective-sensation loss + foot-risk stratification.

ugandaNote: Diabetic + HIV neuropathy + B12 deficiency are common; the diabetic-foot pathway follows loss of protective sensation.

mustCheck.sign: is the forehead spared (UMN) or involved (LMN)?
mustCheck.why: Forehead sparing = UMN (stroke); forehead involved = LMN (Bell's) — the key discriminator.

mustCheck.sign: other cranial nerves + limb signs
mustCheck.why: Associated deficits point to a central/brainstem lesion; isolated LMN VII suggests Bell's.

mustCheck.sign: ear / parotid exam (herpes zoster oticus, parotid mass)
mustCheck.why: Identifies treatable/structural LMN causes.

ugandaNote: Exclude stroke (UMN pattern); HIV can cause Bell's palsy + other cranial neuropathies.

mustCheck.sign: localised vs generalised; all node groups (cervical, axillary, inguinal, epitrochlear, supraclavicular)
mustCheck.why: Distribution reshapes the differential; supraclavicular (Virchow's) suggests intra-abdominal/thoracic malignancy.

mustCheck.sign: node character (size, consistency, tenderness, matting, fixation)
mustCheck.why: Rubbery (lymphoma), hard/fixed (carcinoma), tender (infective), matted (TB).

mustCheck.sign: hepatosplenomegaly
mustCheck.why: Lymphoma/leukaemia + chronic infection present with nodes + organomegaly.

ugandaNote: TB lymphadenitis, HIV (PGL), lymphoma + Kaposi-associated nodes are common — examine for HIV/TB context.

mustCheck.sign: jaundice + signs of haemolysis
mustCheck.why: Pallor + jaundice points to haemolysis (sickle cell, malaria, G6PD).

mustCheck.sign: splenomegaly + chronic liver disease signs
mustCheck.why: Inform the anaemia cause.

mustCheck.sign: koilonychia / glossitis / signs of bleeding or malnutrition
mustCheck.why: Iron deficiency, chronic blood loss, nutritional causes.

ugandaNote: Anaemia is very common (malaria, sickle cell, hookworm/iron deficiency, HIV); severe anaemia is a danger sign needing transfusion access.

mustCheck.sign: hepatomegaly (character/tenderness) + splenomegaly + CLD signs + ascites
mustCheck.why: Distinguishes hepatic/cholestatic from pre-hepatic + detects decompensation.

mustCheck.sign: pallor (haemolysis) + depth/shade of jaundice
mustCheck.why: Pallor + lemon tinge suggests haemolytic (pre-hepatic) jaundice.

mustCheck.sign: Courvoisier's sign (palpable gallbladder) / malignancy signs
mustCheck.why: A palpable non-tender gallbladder + jaundice suggests malignant obstruction.

ugandaNote: Viral hepatitis (A/B/E), malaria (haemolysis), HCC + obstructive causes are common; in pregnancy consider hepatitis E.
